C++23 FRAMEWORK · OPEN SOURCE

C++ graphical
applications
in the age of AI.

WebFront brings together the power of C++ and the graphical possibilities of TypeScript in a complete framework for Windows, macOS and Linux. It supports both the creation of an application and its subsequent evolution.

TypeScript compilation, type checking, preview, automated UI tests and preparation of distributable resources share the same environment. Designed for work with AI agents, WebFront lets you entrust them with an implementation they can build, examine and test.

APPLICATION DEVELOPMENT

An environment for the development lifecycle

Choosing a framework also determines how an application is developed. WebFront provides a common environment for creating the interface, previewing it, checking behaviour and preparing distributable resources. This continuity lets the programme and its presentation evolve without assembling a separate toolchain for each stage.

Create

The project brings together interface sources, a manifest and locked dependencies. C++ functions and presentation components can be designed together from the start of the application.

Develop

The wf terminal compiles TypeScript and TSX. Saving sources updates the preview; an error leaves the last successful version available.

Test and maintain

Type checks and Jasmine journeys accompany changes. An AI harness can request these operations and use their structured results, while the tests remain reusable in CI.

Distribute

wf embed prepares interface resources for inclusion in the C++ programme. The distributed version runs without the development environment; rendering-engine deployment remains platform-specific.

SiliconForge: an application built with WebFront

SiliconForge is currently the only published application using WebFront. This microcontroller simulator was developed around the framework from the outset. It combines a C++ engine with an interface for loading firmware, examining pins and registers, and controlling simulated execution.

Its author reports a particularly rapid development process with WebFront. This experience concerns the construction of a complete application: work on the model, presentation and verification takes place within the same environment.

Explore SiliconForge ↗

Integrating an existing programme

This organisation also suits an existing C++ programme. An interface can be added without imposing a new operating model: computation and data retain their organisation, and the required functions are made accessible to the presentation.

PRINCIPLES

Organisation of a WebFront application

01

The C++ programme

A function registered with cppFunction becomes accessible from TypeScript. The binary bridge transports its arguments and result asynchronously. Application logic can therefore remain independent of presentation.

02

Presentation

An interface can be written in TypeScript, CSS and, where appropriate, React. The same sources serve Windows, macOS and Linux, in a native window or the system browser.

03

Development tools

The wf terminal installs dependencies, compiles TSX sources, checks types and runs tests. wf dev updates the preview whenever a file is saved. These tools require no separate Node.js installation.

04

Distribution

wf embed produces a C++ header containing interface resources and web dependencies. After recompilation, those resources are available offline within the application.

05

Automation

An optional launcher provides type checking, building, testing and limited preview inspection. An AI harness can use it through local MCP or a JSON command-line interface.

WebFront requires a C++23 compiler and C++ dependencies managed by CMake. Rendering uses a browser or web engine: WebView2, WKWebView, WebKitGTK, or optionally CEF. Engine deployment depends on the platform; no JavaScript development environment is required.

PORTABILITY

Supported platforms

WebFront is currently qualified on desktop platforms. A remote browser could also suit some devices, but that use still requires porting and validation.

Windows, macOS and Linux

The examples use a native engine when its dependencies are present, or the system browser. Engine deployment depends on the platform and must be planned with application deployment.

Embedded equipment

Embedded targets and microcontrollers are not qualified. Their C++23 support, available memory and network stack require examination. Remote transport and its security rules remain to be designed and validated.

DEVELOPMENT

Developing the interface in the application window

The WebFrontLifeDeveloper example contains the development terminal. The following commands create the project and open its preview. Edit the TSX and CSS files in your usual editor.

Watch the development session ↗
WEBFRONT TERMINAL
wf create life
wf init
wf install react@19.3.1 react-dom@19.3.1
wf dev ui/main.tsx

AUTOMATION AND TESTING

Evolving an application with a harness

A harness can participate when a screen is first created and throughout subsequent changes: it edits sources, requests type checks and builds, and runs Jasmine journeys. Checks remain with the project for later maintenance. The corresponding chapter describes configuration and the method’s limitations.

The WebFront Book

The book develops an application with WebFront, from its C++ model to distribution. The Game of Life provides an example small enough to study presentation, asynchronous calls, journey tests and work with an AI harness.

Background sections explain the DOM, React components and state, and C++ coroutines and lifetime rules.
